title: Business days across DST and local dates
prompt:
Bug report for schedule.py in the repo root, which adds and counts business days (Monday-Friday, no holidays) for timezone-aware datetimes. Fix add_business_days and business_days_between so they follow the spec below. Python 3.11, standard library only (use zoneinfo; the system tz database is installed, no pip installs).

Run the visible tests from the repo root with: python3 -m unittest -v test_schedule
They only cover a few cases. More cases (several timezones, DST changes, weekends, late-evening times) are checked later, so follow the spec exactly.

Symptoms reported:
1. add_business_days across a DST change shifts the time of day by an hour (09:00 local becomes 10:00 or 08:00).
2. For late-evening datetimes, for example Friday 23:30 in New York (already Saturday in UTC), the result lands on the wrong day or the wrong time of day.
3. business_days_between is off by one for datetimes whose UTC date differs from their local date.

SPEC
Everything works on the LOCAL date of a datetime: the date its own clock shows in the tzinfo it carries (dt.date(), dt.weekday()), never the UTC date.

add_business_days(dt, n)
- dt must be aware (dt.tzinfo is not None and dt.utcoffset() is not None), otherwise ValueError; this is checked for every n, 0 included. n must be an int, otherwise TypeError (1.0, "1", None are rejected, 0.0 too).
- Returns a datetime with the SAME tzinfo object as dt and the SAME local wall-clock time of day (hour, minute, second, microsecond) on the date that is n business days away from dt's local date: later when n > 0, earlier when n < 0. Step one calendar day at a time in that direction and count only Monday-Friday days; dt's own date is not counted. The result is therefore always a business day (unless n == 0).
- dt itself may fall on a weekend: Saturday + 1 and Sunday + 1 are Monday, Saturday - 1 and Sunday - 1 are Friday.
- n == 0 returns dt unchanged, even on a weekend.
- A DST change must not move the wall-clock time: 09:00 local stays 09:00 local across a spring-forward or a fall-back change, only the UTC offset of the result changes. Wall-clock times that do not exist or are ambiguous on the target date (the skipped hour, the repeated hour) are out of scope.

business_days_between(a, b)
- a and b must be aware, otherwise ValueError.
- Counts the Monday-Friday dates d with a_local_date <= d < b_local_date (start inclusive, end exclusive), using a.date() and b.date(), each in its own tzinfo. Time of day is ignored and a and b may be in different timezones.
- When b's local date is before a's, the result is the negative of the count for the reversed range: business_days_between(b, a) == -business_days_between(a, b). Equal local dates give 0.
